title: Classic Rice Salad
subtitle: Long-grain rice with sweetcorn, pepper, cucumber and vinaigrette
excerpt: Long-grain rice with tinned sweetcorn, chopped red pepper, spring onion and cucumber, dressed in a simple vinaigrette. A practical buffet and picnic staple that keeps well and feeds a crowd.
sourceNotes: Rice salad became a standard of British buffet cookery from the 1970s onward, appearing in home economy textbooks and entertaining guides throughout the 1980s. It belongs to the same tradition as potato salad and pasta salad: practical, adaptable, feeds many, and improves with resting time. The combination of rice, sweetcorn, pepper and vinaigrette is the classic British version.

recipe.batchNotes: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge. Add the herbs just before serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the rice and dress it a day ahead. Add the fresh vegetables and herbs close to serving.

content.text: Rice salad is a British buffet staple with a reputation for blandness that it does not entirely deserve. The key is dressing the rice while it is still warm so the grains absorb the vinaigrette, and using enough salt in the cooking water. Cooked and cooled rice is hydrophobic: it will not absorb a dressing applied cold. Warm rice will. The rest is texture: make sure every forkful has crunch from the pepper or cucumber alongside the softness of the grain.

Cook {{long-grain-rice}} of rice in well-salted boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes until just tender. Drain well in a colander and tip into a large bowl while still warm. Whisk together {{olive-oil}} of olive oil, {{white-wine-vinegar}} of white wine vinegar, {{dijon-mustard}} of Dijon mustard, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Pour the dressing over the warm rice and toss to combine. Leave to cool to room temperature, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the sweetcorn, red pepper, cucumber and spring onion. Scatter over the chopped parsley if using. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve at room temperature.

items.fix: Rinse the rice before cooking to remove surface starch. Drain the moment it is just tender; do not overcook.

items.cause: Rice not dressed while warm, or underseasoned cooking water.
items.fix: Cook the rice in well-salted water and dress it the moment it is drained.

content.text: Rice salad belongs to British buffet cooking of the 1970s and 1980s. It sat alongside pasta salads and potato salads on summer tables. It is practical: cheap, it feeds many people, holds on a buffet for a couple of hours, and works with whatever is in the fridge.
